name: Try-Cam Corner
approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, scramble up beneath the long fracture to the base of the rock and work up and right toward the routes above the lake; the approach to this East Buttress is steep. The route goes up the right side of the central pillar of the buttress, starting just left of Manic Laughter, and only reaches the second ledge system.
descent: The line ends on the second ledge, where climbers either continue up another crack system or rappel from slung blocks on the neighbouring Full Metal Jacket line, whose anchors may need fresh cord.
path: Arrowhead < Glacier Gorge < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: Ad Nauseum
approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and take the trail to Emerald Lake (roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way). Go around the left side of the lake, scramble through talus, and pick up a climbers' trail beneath the wall. Ad Nauseum climbs the Third Buttress. It starts beyond the low overhangs that follow the big rockfall scar, and a large left-facing corner is visible overhead. Snow often lingers at the foot of the face early in the season.
overview: Seven pitches with plenty of simul-climbing; the belay with the pin may have been missed, so pitch lengths may be off. P1: Grassy ledges angle up and right to a corner system facing right, 200'+. P2: Traverse right across the face into a long corner
path: Hallett Peak < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado < United States

name: Cowboy Nudes
approach: Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch. Go around the west side of the lake, cross the stream, and climb the short talus slope directly to the wall. The route starts from the midway ledge: reach the ledge by one of the ways described for the Dark Tower, or climb the lower pitches of Raise the Roof. Then walk left along the base of the wall to a short splitter crack at the base of the little gully on the mini-tower to the right of the Dark Tower, besid
descent: Descend the East gully. Walk down the slope of Thatchtop staying fairly close to the North Face; at treeline look for cairns that lead down a big scree and talus slope, and bear a little toward skier's left near the bottom to enter a smaller gully w
overview: Mini-tower right of The Dark Tower's gully (looker's right), from the midway ledge about 400-500 feet up Thatchtop. P1: 5.8, ~180 feet. Start at a ~20' fist/OW splitter, pass white rock, go back left on face and ledge to a brief vertical bit, then up
path: North Face < Thatchtop Mountain < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: Dark Tower, Direct Start
approach: Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch. Go around the west side of the lake, cross the stream, and climb the short talus slope directly to the north face. The Dark Tower is the largest tower on the left of the face, with the Deep Freeze cleft to its left and the Necrophilia gully to its right. The start is in a steep right-facing corner to the left of the giant corner that lies below the left side of the tower; the line crosses that big corner near it
descent: To escape from the midway ledge, head left on the ledge toward the Deep Freeze gully, downclimb several tiers on its left side to a rappel anchor, and rappel to the ground near the start. Continuing up means joining the prow of the Dark Tower.
path: North Face < Thatchtop Mountain < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: The Dark Tower
approach: Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch. Go around the west side of the lake, cross the stream, and head up the short talus slope to the north face. The tower sits on the large ledge that crosses the face at one-third to half height, so first reach the ledge: climb the right-angling weakness to the right of Necrophilia, climb the lower pitches of Raise the Roof and walk left, or take the Direct Start. Then find the prow with the splitter crack.
descent: Rappel off the back of the tower to a level area, then either scramble up to the ridgeline for one of the walk-offs or cross to the head of the Deep Freeze rappels.
overview: Prow climb on the face of Thatchtop that looks north over Loch Vale, starting from the long midway ledge. Reach it by a 200' weakness right of Necrophilia (easy 5th to 5.6), Raise the Roof (5.8) up to its third belay, or the Direct Start (5.10 R). P1
path: North Face < Thatchtop Mountain < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: Humdinger
approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge Junction trailhead, or ride the shuttle to it, and follow the Glacier Gorge trail past Mills Lake to Black Lake. Above the lake, head east on a faint path to treeline, then cut back south across slabs and meadows to the foot of the Spearhead's main southeast face. The route is the leftmost line on that face, with Border Patrol starting around the corner to its left.
path: Spearhead < Glacier Gorge < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: The Stoneman
approach: Trails from the Glacier Gorge trailhead lead to Black Lake. At Stoneman Pass, go east along the divide's south side toward Chiefshead to the conspicuous tower, walk beyond it, and descend northward. Downclimb north to the tower's east side, then use third- and fourth-class ground to swing round to the northeast side and enter a gully. Belay anywhere; climbing to near the summit makes the belay simpler.
overview: From the northeast gully, fourth-class and fifth-class ground leads to two cracks for the hands. The right one went at 5.6 and the left appears slightly harder; an easier option is to remain on the right and angle back left later. Past the cracks, wo
path: Stoneman Pass < Glacier Gorge < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: The Stumbling Stone
approach: From the Granite Lake trailhead hike to the southern end of the lake and circle it to the far end, where a peninsula has a primitive campsite. Stay to climber's right of the feature called Thunderdome and follow the obvious gully and snow slope. Look for a big block that has partly pulled away from the wall, with a ramp running up on its right; the route starts at the crack where the block meets the cliff, or up the ramp.
path: Northeast Face < 'A' Peak < Cabinet Mountain Wilderness < Northwest Region

name: Backpack
approach: Park at the northern end of the Wapack Trail and hike south on it to the summit of North Pack. From there head east on the Cliff Trail, passing the Carolyn's Trail junction, until you reach the top of the cliff with the Pack Monadnock fire tower in view. Walk down and around the cliff through the scree field to its base. Backpack takes the ramp-like gully with Pack a Punch on one side and Pack it Out on the other.
descent: The top of the cliff carries no bolts or rappel stations. The way down is the walk around the cliff through the scree field, and a rappel from natural anchors is a second option.
overview: Now somewhat overgrown. Follow the ramp gully to a block of quartz, then step right and belay from a tree, or keep going along the arete to the cliff top.
path: North Pack Monadnock < Monadnock Region < New Hampshire < United States

name: Silk Road
approach: Starting at Fairy Meadows, hike to the foot of the tower; a snowfield lies on the way. Its first pitch begins roughly 100 feet to the right of the starting chimney of the Southeast Face.
path: Lotus Flower Tower < Mackenzie Mountains < Northwest Territories < Canada

name: Raise the Drawbridge!
approach: Access is a flight to Qikiqtarjuaq, then a chartered boat or a sea kayak trip from there. Follow the north arm of the Coronation Glacier up. The line starts where rock emerges from the ice on the glacier's north margin, and a water-filled moat separates the rock from the ice; crossing it takes a swim in a dry suit or a Tyrolean traverse rigged from the far side.
descent: Descent is by rappelling the route with two ropes, from gear anchors, slung horns and one single-bolt anchor, so carry extra gear to supplement them. A walk-off may be possible down one of several gullies west of the route.
path: Coronation Glacier < East Coast < Baffin Island < Nunavut

name: Sultans of Slander
approach: Find the climbers' trail just east of the Highline trail parking lot and follow it to the base of the main Iron Hayden wall. Traverse north along the base until a short rocky ridge blocks the way, descend a short distance, and keep traversing the base of a short wall into the Hayden Couloir. Cross over the couloir to the skyline arete, then scramble up to its base. The route is on a tower formation a short way right of Estwing Arete.
descent: Rappel the route.
overview: P1 (5.9, 100'): follow the bolts, some with homemade hangers; quality drops after the first 50', with rambling over ledges to a big ledge anchored by 2 bolts. Something of a junk pitch, yet preferable to hiking. P2 (3rd class, 70'): scramble up and t
path: Estwing Crag, The < Hayden Peak < Uinta Mountains < Northeast Utah

name: Artic Rose
approach: Take US-2 east from Seattle/Everett over Stevens Pass, then drop onto the old Stevens Pass Highway (now Tye Rd), which heads toward the Iron Horse Trailhead and the Wellington townsite; park in the pullout just uphill of a double hairpin turn roughly 1.4 miles from US-2. From there, the on-foot approach follows only faint boot-path traces through open old-growth forest, generally trending uphill and left across a drainage to reach the base of the crag. Expect about 1,000 feet of elevation gain a
descent: Single 85-foot rappel from fixed anchors. Rappel directly down the fixed anchors to return to base.
overview: The easiest route on Half Moon Crag, offering perfect intro to the area with positive holds and excellent protection throughout.
path: Half Moon Crag < Skykomish Valley < Central-West Cascades & Seattle < Washington

approach: This crag's coordinates correspond to the Hannegan Pass/Ruth Creek Valley area near Mt. Baker, sometimes referenced as 'Ellation Crags,' a minor, lightly-developed granite cragging/multipitch area. The general access is from I-5 Exit 255, east on SR-542 (Mt. Baker Highway) about 46 miles, then a left onto Forest Road 32 (Hannegan Pass Road) for about 4 miles to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead. Beyond that trailhead, published approach details for the crag itself are sparse and inconsistent, so the e

overview: A single-pitch handcrack splitting a large, thin rock flake up the center of the crag — sustained, well-protected trad climbing to a chain anchor.

name: Glacier View Palace
approach: Hike up, around and above Glacier View Temple to reach the route, which sits atop Enchanting Puller Blind.
descent: Lower from the chain anchor. Single lower from the top; short route within any standard rope length.
overview: Dirty jugs on white-stained rock atop Enchanting Puller Blind, with notably better bolt condition than its harder neighbor.
path: East Face < Keechelus Ridge < Snoqualmie Pass Area < Central-West Cascades & Seattle

name: Half Fast
approach: Take US-2 east from Seattle/Everett over Stevens Pass, then drop onto the old Stevens Pass Highway (now Tye Rd), which heads toward the Iron Horse Trailhead and the Wellington townsite; park in the pullout just uphill of a double hairpin turn roughly 1.4 miles from US-2. overview: A solid moderate route with good flow and continuous climbing on slab and crack. Excellent for building confidence.

name: Miracle Ramps
approach: From the grassy saddle bivy, ascend class 4 ramps to a dihedral, then to the starting wall ledge shared with Primal Scream.
descent: Rappel the route 6 rappels down the route via two-bolt stainless in-line chain anchors.
overview: A 6-pitch variation of the first six pitches of the older Primal Scream, up the right side of a central buttress on the South Face, finishing at its own summit anchor.
path: South Face < Squire Creek Walls < Darrington < Darrington and Mountain Loop Hwy

name: Moss Out For Harambe
approach: From the Barlow Pass gate, walk the closed road (old railroad grade) approximately 4 miles to the Monte Cristo townsite; a backcountry campground sits at that mark. Mossy Loaf's coordinates place it essentially at/immediately adjacent to the townsite itself, so once at the flat of Monte Cristo the formation is only a short distance further off the main townsite path. The exact final spur to the specific wall is not well established, so on-site scouting is recommended for the last stretch.
descent: Walk off along the base of the tiers back to the roadside; no fixed rappel anchor is documented for this single-pitch line. From the top of the route, downclimb the easy slab above the crux or scramble off along the wall's edge back to road level. Th
overview: A one-pitch 5.7 trad line up Mossy Loaf's upper tier, climbing an open-book past a distinctive 'monkey face' rock feature to a roof, then a steep lieback flake crux before easing off on slab.
path: Mossy Loaf < Monte Cristo Townsite < Darrington and Mountain Loop Hwy < Northwest Region

name: Nature's Way
approach: From the grassy saddle bivy, cross the granite apron past the start of Concerto in C for Drill and Hammer to two-bolt ring anchors on the opposite wall.
descent: Rappel the route 3 rappels down the route via two-bolt chain anchors at each belay.
overview: A short, 3-pitch line finishing up an obvious hand crack soaring above the South Face's granite apron - the most recently established named route on the wall.
path: South Face < Squire Creek Walls < Darrington < Darrington and Mountain Loop Hwy

name: NE Arete
approach: From the Cutthroat Trailhead (~4,500 ft, via SR-20 and FS Road 400 about 28 miles west of Winthrop), follow the Cutthroat Creek Trail/PCT toward Cutthroat Pass, then branch onto scree slopes to reach the base of the NE Face/NE Arete.
overview: Molar Tooth's original 1971 first-ascent line, climbing the crest of the northeast arete at a moderate 5.6 to the summit.
path: Molar Tooth < Cutthroat Lake Crags < Washington Pass < North Cascades

name: NE Chimney
approach: From the Cutthroat Trailhead (~4,500 ft, via SR-20 and FS Road 400 about 28 miles west of Winthrop), follow the Cutthroat Creek Trail/PCT toward Cutthroat Pass, then branch onto scree slopes to reach the base of the NE Face.
overview: A harder, sustained line up a chimney system on Molar Tooth's NE Face, rated 5.9.
path: Molar Tooth < Cutthroat Lake Crags < Washington Pass < North Cascades

name: Nest Route
approach: From Randle, WA (Hwy 12), head south on Hwy 131, keep right and follow NF-25 for 19.2 miles. After milepost 21, turn left at the sign for Mosquito Meadows onto NF-28 and follow it for 2.7 miles, then turn left onto NF-77. Continue on this rough, high-clearance-recommended road for about 2 miles until Pinto Rock comes into view, then continue to the large pullout where the main climber's trail is clearly visible. From the pullout, walk up the road toward the wall to reach the base of the West Fac

overview: The North Face of The Mole (Edward Peak, 7,280 ft) is an amazing alpine rock route offering 500 feet of easy, adventurous 5.7 climbing on the tallest of a quartet of granite spires at the northern fringe of the Enchantments, with unique views of the

overview: A short, easy one-pitch 5.5 that traverses under a small roof to a good crimp then eases up slab; used by some parties mainly as a lower-impact way to reach Mossy Loaf's upper tier.

name: Zool Patch
approach: Same approach as Clean Break: from Washington Pass, drive east on SR-20 to either the Silver Star Creek pullout (~8.5 miles) or the Wine Spires pullout (~4 miles), then hike/traverse to the east face of Juno Tower. Zool Patch starts about 150 feet left of Clean Break's start.
descent: Two double-rope rappels straight down from the double bail trees atop pitch 4. From the anchors at the top of pitch 4 (double bail trees), make two consecutive double-rope rappels straight down the line of the route back to the base.
overview: A shorter, little-traveled 4-pitch line up double cracks and an offwidth flake 150 feet left of Clean Break on Juno Tower's east face, finishing with a brushy leftward traverse and two rappels back to the ground.
path: Juno Tower < Silver Star and Wine spires < Washington Pass < North Cascades

name: Where's Bernie?
approach: The route is in Boy Scout Cirque in Teton Canyon, at the far right side of the cirque, beyond the Boy Scout couloir and the big roof dihedrals. It follows a diagonal crack to a left-facing dihedral.
descent: Descend by rappel from the sling anchors at the top of the climb; a single rope is enough to reach the ground.
overview: Expect loose, crumbling rock in quantity, with suspect blocks. Climb the diagonal crack (5.9) up into the dihedral facing left (5.9/10a). Protection is good the whole way. Anchors are slings. A single 60m rope gets you down.
path: Boy Scout Cirque Route List < Teton Canyon < Wyoming < United States

name: North Ridge
approach: Walk north from Pahaska on service roads and ski trails, cross the creek, and follow the Crow Creek trail west. When due north of the peak, turn south through brush to a meadow with log crossings, then follow a faint trail to the big avalanche gully below the north ridge. Stay just right of the gully to avoid the worst brush, pass a cliff band, and climb the steep couloir of snow or talus to the ridge; an ice axe and crampons are needed when it holds snow. Traverse southwest across the base of t
descent: Descend the standard east face rappel line, which uses slung horns and pins for anchors.
overview: Scramble over the basaltic ridge base (class 3 and 4) and along sloping ledges toward the NW face to the start ledge, which is 100m SW of the N Ridge crest. Several options, each 2-3 ropelengths at 5.7, reach the northern end of the long hogsback; st
path: Cody Peak < Absaroka Range < Wyoming < United States

name: Barf Ceiling (Strawberry Alarm Clock)
approach: Start at the Lake Marie recreation area beside Wyoming 130, the Snowy Range Road, which is a seasonal road. A faint path leaves the picnic ground and runs to the foot of the scree, then you choose your own line over the talus to the cliff. Snow and ice often linger at the base into early summer, so an ice axe and crampons are useful in early season. The route is the roof at the far right end of the Little Diamond, the first line right of Guillotine.
overview: Found in the far right corner of the Little Diamond. Climb directly up the roof, passing the pair of giant blocks on either side.
path: Medicine Bow Peak Area < Snowy Range < Wyoming < United States

name: Captain Morgan

A faint path leaves the picnic ground and runs to the foot of the scree, then you choose your own line over the talus to the cliff. Snow and ice often linger at the base into early summer, so an ice axe and crampons are useful in early season. The line starts 100 feet right of Cornerless, in the middle of a smooth pointed buttress.
overview: Begin at the foot of the face, 100 feet to the right of Cornerless and midway across a pointed buttress of smooth white rock. Climb to Flat Ledge, step left to an offwidth, then follow a diagonal line crossing overhangs.
path: Medicine Bow Peak Area < Snowy Range < Wyoming < United States

name: Cornerless

The line is the first one right of the pillar on the right side of the wall, and it goes up to the anchors on the Flat Ledge.
overview: Lies immediately right of the pillar, on Diamond Wall Right, heading directly to the Flat Ledge anchors. A huge red dihedral once stood here, but that ten-story feature has since collapsed.

name: Diamond Cutter

name: Duncan's Lieback

The start is at the left end of the Flat Ledge, just right of the bolts, and the first pitch is the Cornerless line up to that ledge.

name: Flying Cojone Brothers

Snow and ice often linger at the base into early summer, so an ice axe and crampons are useful in early season. The route begins from the Flat Ledge, which you reach by climbing Cornerless.
overview: Leaving Flat Ledge, ascend M&M Diagonal until you are ten feet under the overhangs. Then cut ten feet left and pass the roof via its thin crack.
path: Medicine Bow Peak Area < Snowy Range < Wyoming < United States

name: Guillotine

The route is on the left of the two big overhangs at the far right end of the Little Diamond.

name: Summer Solstice

The route leaves the Flat Ledge on the first major right-leaning diagonal right of Captain Morgan.

name: The Living Stone
approach: This is a long backcountry trip of roughly 14 to 16 miles each way from the Big Sandy trailhead, with Hailey Pass crossed in the later part of the walk. The trail ends among the boulders and meadows below the wall, and parties usually camp right at its foot. The other way in is from the Dickinson Park side. The route is on the northeast face, to the left of Gambling in the Winds, and the wall below it is reached across the boulder field.

name: Kamp Krusty
approach: Springfield Gully is a short walk from the camp in the Cirque of the Towers, in the cuts of the buttress at the edge of camp, below the Watchtower. A climbers' path from the campsites runs under the gentle slabs on both sides; most of the routes here lie in the left-hand cut. Walk up the gully to a hidden wall on the south side, where Kamp Krusty is the largest continuous crack.
descent: Rappel from the gear anchor to climber's left, down the narrow gap beside the crack.

name: The Pretender
approach: From the Caves camp, take the main trail toward the Lower Saddle, cross the creek that drains the Teepe Glacier, and take the trail toward the glacier and the guide-service camp. Walk part of the way up toward the glacier, ford the creek a second time and hop boulders to the foot of the tower, which is on your right. The route is on the left of the line called Good over Evil, keeping to the ridge.
descent: The tower can be descended by rappelling off the top on the side facing the meadows.
overview: Protection is great. A couple of added 1s and 3s on a single rack would not hurt. Expect some vegetation low down.

They are guarded by Windy Arm, which is crossed by boat or paddle (on skis or foot in winter) to the mouth of Ramshorn Creek. From the alluvial fan, find a way through the trees, burn and meadows to the towers; no trail exists.
